description: Local UI to run and train LLMs and diffusion models. Supports GGUF, MLX, Qwen3.8, DeepSeek-V4.1, MiniMax-H3, Gemma 4, FLUX and more.

sources.entry: unsloth - Faster, lower-memory LLM fine-tuning, as a Python library or a desktop app.

summary.one_liner: Unsloth is a local desktop app, web UI (Unsloth Studio), and Python library for running, fine-tuning, and exporting LLMs and diffusion models.
summary.what_it_does: Unsloth provides a desktop app, a browser-based Studio UI launched with `unsloth studio`, and a code-based Python package (Unsloth Core) for running and training models. The README says it runs LLMs, MLX, GGUF, diffusion, audio, and embedding models, and it lists several model families such as Qwen3.8, DeepSeek-V4, Gemma 4, and FLUX. For training, it covers LoRA, QLoRA, full fine-tuning, pretraining, RL, GRPO, DPO, and FP8, and it claims 2x speed and 70% less VRAM with no accuracy loss. It can export or deploy models in GGUF, NVFP4, and FP8 formats, and build datasets from PDFs, CSVs, and DOCX files via Data Recipes. It also includes "Unsloth Start," a command that connects agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode to local models, and it serves an OpenAI-compatible API with optional Cloudflare HTTPS remote access.
use_cases: run local LLMs on my own machine
fine-tune a model with LoRA or QLoRA
train diffusion or image models locally
connect Claude Code or Codex to a local model
export a fine-tuned model to GGUF
build training datasets from PDFs and CSVs
how_to_run: curl -fsSL https://unsloth.ai/install.sh | sh  (macOS, Linux, WSL; URL truncated in README)
irm https://unsloth.ai/install.ps1 | iex  (Windows PowerShell; URL truncated in README)
uv pip install unsloth --torch-backend=auto  (Unsloth Core, code-based)
notable: Three ways to use it: native desktop app, Unsloth Studio web UI, or code-based Unsloth Core library
Unsloth Start connects Claude Code, Codex, VS Code, OpenCode and other agents to local models with one command
Supports NVIDIA, AMD, Intel GPUs, CPUs, multi-GPU, and Vulkan backend
Remote access via a free Cloudflare HTTPS link or LAN access
Dual license: core package Apache-2.0, Studio UI under AGPL-3.0
caveats: Server-side tools are enabled by default when exposed; the README warns to set a password or use --disable-tools
Windows installs need torchao installed first for an up-to-date Unsloth; a one-step install can resolve an old version
AMD, Intel, and Blackwell setups point to separate guides and images
Some install URLs are truncated in the README text, so exact commands should be checked on the source page
